title: Constant Force Motion in One Dimension
learningObjectives: Use net force and mass to calculate acceleration in one dimension
Predict velocity and displacement over time for constant net force and constant mass

explanations.text: Acceleration equals net force divided by mass, expressed as F = m*a.

evidence.quote: The force (F) will be the difference between the opposing forces (thrust minus drag).
However, if the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.

explanations.text: In one direction the net force is thrust minus drag, and unbalanced forces cause motion toward the greater force.

evidence.quote: For a constant force and constant mass, the acceleration remains constant.

explanations.text: With constant force and constant mass, acceleration stays constant and velocity changes linearly with time.

evidence.quote: we will consider only the horizontal (x-direction) motion

explanations.text: For horizontal motion, position depends on acceleration, time squared, initial velocity, and initial position.

behavioralTests.name: zero net force gives zero acceleration
